# Ultimate Planner 2027 — User Guide

A complete digital planner for OneNote and PDF note-taking apps:
- yearly goals
- 12 monthly sections (calendar, goals, reflection)
- 53 weekly trackers
- 111 professional templates in 10 categories
- 8 note layouts

Every page is linked from a General Index.

## What's included

| Part | Pages |
|---|---|
| Start: General Index, How to use, Yearly Goals, Year at a Glance, Resources | 5 |
| 12 monthly sections: Calendar · Goals · Reflection | 36 |
| Weekly Tracker (priorities, top 3 goals, daily plan, appointments, habits, notes, achievements, reflection) | 53 + contents |
| Task Management templates | 9 |
| Project Management templates | 29 |
| Meeting Notes templates | 8 |
| Goal Setting templates | 8 |
| Time Management templates | 7 |
| Professional Development templates | 16 |
| Client & Customer Tracking templates | 9 |

| Notes (General, Quick, Research, Meeting, Reading, Project, Ideas, Personal Reflection) | 8 |

Each template category and the Notes and Weekly sections start with a contents page that links to every page in it.

## Which file do I use?

| You use | Use this |
|---|---|
| **OneNote for Windows** (Microsoft 365 / OneNote desktop) | `Ultimate_Planner_2027.onepkg`: double-click it and choose where to save the notebook |
| **OneNote for Mac, web, iPad** | The PDF planner: insert it into a OneNote page (see below) |
| **GoodNotes, Notability, Xodo, Drawboard, Samsung Notes** | `Ultimate_Planner_2027_Hyperlinked.pdf`: open or import it; the tabs and index links are clickable |
| **Paper** | Print the PDF (landscape, "fit to page") |

> The `.onepkg` notebook file opens in OneNote for Windows. Other versions of OneNote can't open .onepkg files; that's a Microsoft limitation, so use the PDF there.

## Using the OneNote notebook

1. Double-click `Ultimate_Planner_2027.onepkg`. OneNote asks where to keep the notebook; pick OneDrive to sync it to your phone.
2. Open the **Start** section › **General Index**. Click any link to jump to that page.
3. Click **⌂ Index** at the top of any page to come back.
4. Tick checkboxes by clicking them. Press **Tab** in the last cell of a table to add a row.
5. To reuse a template: right-click the page in the page list › **Copy**, then right-click › **Paste**. Rename the copy.

The notebook is organised in OneNote like this:
- **Start:** index, how to use, yearly goals, year at a glance, resources
- **Months:** 12 sections, January–December
- **Weekly Tracker**
- **Templates:** 10 sections
- **Notes**

## Using the PDF in OneNote (Mac, Windows, web)

- **Windows / Mac:** open a blank page › **Insert › File Printout** (Mac: **Insert › PDF Printout**) and choose the PDF. Each planner page becomes a page background you can type or draw on.
- **Tip:** create one OneNote section per month and insert only the pages you need. Printouts are images, so links inside them don't click in OneNote. Use OneNote's own page list to move around.

## Using the PDF in GoodNotes, Notability and other apps

- Import the PDF as a new notebook or document.
- **Navigation:** the tabs on the left of every page and every index/contents link are clickable in read or link mode. ⌂ Index is at the top right of every page.
- Write with your pen or type in text boxes. Duplicate a template page to reuse it.

## Tips

- In the 2027 edition, week pages are dated Monday to Sunday (ISO weeks). Week 53 is a spare page; fill in your own dates.
- The undated edition has the same 226 pages with blank calendar grids and week dates: start any month, reuse it any year.
- Colour code: each section has its own colour, used on the index and on that section's pages.
- Search everything in OneNote with **Ctrl+E** (Mac: **Cmd+Option+F**).

## FAQ

**Can I use it for another year?** Yes. Use `Ultimate_Planner_Undated_Hyperlinked.pdf`: the same planner with blank dates on the calendars and weekly pages. In the 2027 edition, the 111 templates and 8 note pages are undated too.

**Can I change colours or add pages?** Yes. In OneNote everything is editable: add rows and pages, rename sections, change colours.

**Links don't work after I moved pages.** Links follow the page, not its position, so moving pages is fine. If you *copied* the notebook to a new place with a different tool, re-link with **Ctrl+K**.

**Is there a Mac version?** Use the PDF in OneNote for Mac (Insert › PDF Printout), or in any PDF note app.
